messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 planning: OKR alignment council — proposal, owners, and sign-off

Team —

Attached is the first-pass OKR package for the upcoming quarter (okr-2026-q3-draft.xlsx) plus a one-pager that highlights the cross-functional asks. High-level goals: tighten inference reliability, reduce per-token cost for embedded workloads, and surface productized observability for Dedicated customers.

Ask: please review the KRs and owners in the spreadsheet and add inline comments to the Drive doc by EOD Wed (Aug 4). In particular:
- Engineering: confirm feasibility/timeline for KR infra-1 (99.9% p95 for hosted API) and KR infra-2 (Dedicated SLA target).
- Product: validate customer-facing success metrics and which flows to instrument for QBR.
- GTM: confirm go-to-market targets and any dependencies on pricing/credits.

I've listed provisional owners in column D. If you want to reassign, add a note directly. Planning notes and a short runbook for the QBR deck (qbr-runbook.pptx) are linked in the Drive doc.

Attachments: okr-2026-q3-draft.xlsx, okr-one-pager.pdf, qbr-runbook.pptx

Thanks —
Ava
Ava Chen | Head of Strategy, Redwood Inference

----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 planning: OKR alignment council — proposal, owners, and sign-off

Thanks, Ava — quick notes from infra.

I reviewed the KRs. Two items to call out:
1) KR infra-1 (p95 latency target for hosted) — current rollout plan (kernel opt + batching) lines up but the KR as written has a 100ms target which is optimistic for mixed-length inference. Recommend changing to p95 <= 140ms and adding a stretch KR at p95 <= 120ms.
2) Dedicated SLA (KR infra-2) — suggested SLA: 99.95% for sustained capacity; for initial launch we should offer 99.9% with an upgrade path. That should be reflected in the wording.

I added inline comments in the Drive sheet and attached a short note (infra-impact-notes.txt) that maps code/infra work to KRs. If Product can sign off on the SLA wording, we can commit headcount and schedule.

On owners: I'm OK owning infra-1 and infra-2 execution; please move the owner cell accordingly.

— Marcus
CTO, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the draft — left product-side edits. Summary of changes I made in the Drive doc:
- Objective: "Deliver predictable inference economics for production apps" (slightly reworded to be customer-facing).
- KR1: reduce median per-token cost for embeddings by 20% (measured via token-cost dashboard).
- KR2: 2 pilot customers on Dedicated with GA pricing committed (assigned to Grace).
- KR3: roll out observability baseline (latency + token-cost per route) to 80% of active routes.

I've proposed the following owners:
- KR1: Product + Benchmarking (owner: monica.patel)
- KR2: GTM (owner: grace.oconnor)
- KR3: Engineering (owner: marcus.lin, execution lead: samir.kapoor) — noted Samir in the doc (Samir is on infra team).

Attached: okr-one-pager.pdf (customer-facing summary). I also added a short note on measurement approach in the Drive file. Marcus — agree with moving infra owner cells to you. Grace — can you confirm the two pilot accounts you want to target? I recommended Acme as one of them (Matt Sullivan is open to a pilot conversation).

Thanks —
Monica
VP Product, Redwood Inference

Thanks, team — solid work. I reviewed the updated Drive doc and the one-pager. Two quick edits before we lock:
1) Make the Dedicated SLA language explicit that initial public launch is 99.9% with a roadmap to 99.95% within two quarters.
2) On the customer success KR (pilot commitments), make the acceptance criteria clearer: signed statement of work or signed pilot agreement.

Ava — please incorporate those two edits and publish the final worksheet. Sign-off from me here; we can treat this as the formal OKR package once updated.

Vivek Kulkarni
CEO, Redwood Inference
